title: task edit rejects --implementation-notes, the name task create uses for the same field, and the rejection does not say the rest of the command was discarded
description:
Reported by opum-agent 2026-09-18, primary measurement by opum-doc on ODOC-241. Measured here before judging, and the measurement narrows the report in two ways worth recording.

WHAT IS REAL. quest task create writes implementationNotes with --implementation-notes. quest task edit writes the SAME FIELD with --notes. Verified end to end: create --implementation-notes and edit --notes both land in .data.implementationNotes. So this is a NAMING asymmetry for one field, not a missing capability, and the discoverable name differs between the two commands that a caller uses in sequence on the same record.

WHAT THE REPORT OVERSTATED, checked rather than accepted. It said nothing in the output names which flag was rejected. The message does name it, prominently and first: Unrecognized flag --implementation-notes. Accepted flags: ... and that list already contains --notes and --add-note. So the discoverability half is largely already served; the genuine gap is narrower.

THE GENUINE GAP. The rejection does not say that the REST of the command was discarded. opum-docs invocation paired --check-ac 6 with the bad flag, and the observable outcome was an acceptance criterion silently not checked. Atomicity is correct and is not being changed; what is missing is that the message never tells the caller the valid flags did not apply either. Exit 2 and nothing written, both confirmed by probe.

WHAT IS NOT IN SCOPE, and why. The reports other cited instance, --reference on create versus --add-reference/--remove-reference on edit, is a DIFFERENT shape: edit deliberately offers non-destructive add/remove and no wholesale replacement. DEC-5 recorded the hazard of wholesale replacement discarding state on a neighbouring field, so adding a wholesale --references to edit would reintroduce exactly the trap DEC-5 refused. Not treating the two as one class.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest task edit accepts --implementation-notes and writes the same implementationNotes field that --notes writes, verified by asserting the two spellings produce an identical record rather than by reading the flag list
Supplying both --notes and --implementation-notes in one edit is rejected rather than silently preferring one, so the alias cannot become a new silent-loss path
The unrecognized-flag message states that the rest of the command was not applied, and a test asserts both the naming of the rejected flag and the discard sentence
Atomicity is unchanged: a rejected edit still writes nothing and still exits 2, asserted directly
No wholesale --references is added to task edit, and the reason is recorded rather than left as an omission

implementationNotes:
MEASURED BEFORE JUDGING, and the measurement narrowed the report. The claim that nothing in the output names the rejected flag is not right: the message led with Unrecognized flag --implementation-notes and listed every accepted flag including --notes and --add-note. So the discoverability half was largely served already. The genuine gap was narrower and is the one fixed: the message never said the VALID flags in the same invocation had not applied either, which is what made a discarded --check-ac look like a checkbox that silently failed to check.

Also narrowed the CLASS. The report treated --implementation-notes and --reference as two members of one asymmetry class. They are different: --implementation-notes vs --notes is the SAME capability under two names, while --reference vs --add-reference/--remove-reference is a deliberate shape difference -- edit offers non-destructive add/remove and no wholesale replacement. DEC-5 recorded what wholesale replacement costs on a neighbouring field, so adding --references to edit would reintroduce the trap DEC-5 refused. Fixed the first, declined the second, and pinned the decline with a test so the omission reads as a decision rather than an oversight.

MUTATION PROOF, three mutations, each predicted to redden exactly ONE test and each measured doing so. M1 drop the both-spellings guard: only test 2. M2 drop the discard sentence from the message: only test 3. M3 accept the alias but do not wire it to the field: only test 1 -- the subtle failure where a flag is accepted, the command exits 0, and nothing reaches the record.

PROCEDURE CORRECTION MADE MID-PROOF, and it belongs here because it is the sessions own theme again. My first M1 run printed a site count I misread as the mutation having failed to apply; there was an unrelated second occurrence of the matched string elsewhere in the file. The result was right and my reading of the evidence was wrong. I then re-ran M3 with an explicit diff assertion that the mutant DIFFERS from the original before interpreting any test result, because a mutation that silently did not apply produces a run that is ambiguous between the test being weak and the mutation never having happened -- the same absent-versus-negative confusion as the uniform-null trap, wearing process clothes. Verify the mutant applied before trusting the verdict.

A PRE-EXISTING TEST CAUGHT A REAL OMISSION. QCLI-147s contract test requires task edit help to document every flag it accepts. Adding --implementation-notes to the accepted list without adding it to the help entry turned that test red immediately. That is the gate working as designed and is why the alias is documented rather than merely accepted.

SESSION HANDOFF, written ahead of recycle at orchestrator instruction. This session is over its context budget; the boundary set was land PR #197 then stop. PR #197 landed as d006acf.

PROMOTION STATE, and it is READY, not owed. At handoff time origin/dev carries three commits ahead of origin/main: ce6a9e7 (QCLI-342), f5742d4 (QCLI-343), d006acf (QCLI-344), plus this handoff commit. Promotion PR #198 is open from dev to main and its head moves with this commit. All three required contexts (source-gates, Tracker integrity, lore check) must be green on the FINAL head before pushing; the push is git push origin origin/dev:main, never the merge button. If a successor finds #198 still open, that is the only outstanding action in this repository and nothing else is half-finished. The earlier gap the orchestrator flagged at 18:14:59Z is this same set, not a separate one.

QCLI-344 CONCLUSION, recorded so it is not re-derived. Atomicity is CORRECT and was never the defect: a rejected edit writes nothing and exits 2, both asserted. The gap was that the message never said the VALID flags in the same invocation had also not applied, which made a discarded --check-ac look like a checkbox that silently failed. Fixed in the message only. Separately, the report treated --implementation-notes and --reference as one asymmetry class; they are not. The first is one capability under two names and is now aliased. The second is a deliberate SHAPE difference -- task edit offers non-destructive --add-reference/--remove-reference and no wholesale replacement -- and adding a wholesale --references would reintroduce exactly the destructive-replacement trap DEC-5 refused. Declined and pinned with a test so the omission reads as a decision.

WITHDRAWN, DO NOT PICK UP. The orchestrator asked whether the --json error envelope is correct as-is given that a caller selecting fields out of .data gets uniform nulls at exit 0 on a rejected write, then explicitly withdrew the question and released this session from answering. A successor should NOT treat it as inherited work. If it ever returns, the material already exists: QCLI-342 documented that success and error are two shapes sharing no payload key, that the record is under data, and that a caller should branch on the exit code -- which is the contract answer -- and added the print-the-key-set remedy to the guide. Nothing further was promised.

WHAT I WOULD HAVE SENT AND NOW WILL NOT. Only the above plus an acknowledgement of theirs. No open question was left with any peer, and no peer is waiting on this repository for anything.

NOT STARTED, NOT OWED, RECORDED ONLY SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED AS A GAP: the lint over evidence-bearing prose for field names absent from the producing source, named in the CLAUDE.md profile section. It remains uncommissioned by design, with a fourth instance after the fleet-level record as the agreed trigger for revisiting. Do not build it speculatively.
finalSummary:
task edit now accepts --implementation-notes, the name task create uses for the same field, and a rejected flag now says the rest of the command was not applied.

WHAT CHANGED. Three things, all small. --implementation-notes is accepted on task edit as an alias of --notes and wired to the same implementationNotes field. Supplying BOTH is refused with a usage error rather than silently preferring one, so the alias cannot become a new way to lose a write -- the failure mode DEC-5 exists to prevent on a neighbouring field. And the unrecognized-flag message now reads: Unrecognized flag X. Nothing was written: the rest of this command was not applied either. Accepted flags: ...

WHAT THE REPORT OVERSTATED, measured rather than accepted. It said nothing in the output names which flag was rejected. The message already led with the rejected flag and listed every accepted one including --notes. The real gap was that it never said the VALID flags alongside it had also not applied, which is what made opum-docs discarded --check-ac look like a checkbox that silently failed rather than a command that never ran.

WHAT WAS DECLINED AND WHY. The report treated --implementation-notes and --reference as one asymmetry class. They are not. --implementation-notes versus --notes is one capability under two names. --reference versus --add-reference/--remove-reference is a deliberate shape difference: edit offers non-destructive add/remove and no wholesale replacement, and DEC-5 recorded exactly what wholesale replacement costs. Adding --references to edit would reintroduce the trap DEC-5 refused. Declined, and pinned with a test so the omission reads as a decision.

ATOMICITY IS UNCHANGED AND WAS NOT THE DEFECT. A rejected edit still writes nothing and still exits 2, both asserted directly. The fix is to the message, not the behaviour.

HOW IT WAS VERIFIED. bun run check exits 0, 589 pass 0 fail. Four new tests spawn the real CLI and assert the two spellings produce IDENTICAL RECORDS rather than comparing flag lists. Three mutations, each predicted to redden exactly one test and each measured doing so: dropping the both-spellings guard reddens only test 2; dropping the discard sentence reddens only test 3; accepting the alias without wiring it reddens only test 1, which is the subtle failure where a flag is accepted, the command exits 0, and nothing reaches the record.

A PRE-EXISTING GATE CAUGHT A REAL OMISSION: QCLI-147s contract test requires task edit help to document every accepted flag, and went red the moment the alias was accepted but not documented. That is why the alias is documented rather than merely accepted.

PROCEDURE NOTE. One mutation result was initially misread because a matched string had an unrelated second occurrence in the file. Re-ran with an explicit diff assertion that the mutant differs from the original before interpreting any verdict, since a mutation that silently did not apply gives a run that is ambiguous between a weak test and an absent mutation. Same absent-versus-negative confusion as this sessions uniform-null thread, in process form.
